'''''The Dog Stars''''' is a 2026 [[post apocalyptic|post-apocalyptic]] [[action thriller]] film directed and produced by [[Ridley Scott]], from a screenplay by [[Mark L. Smith]], based on [[The Dog Stars|the 2012 novel]] by [[Peter Heller (writer)|Peter Heller]]. The film stars [[Jacob Elordi]], [[Josh Brolin]], [[Margaret Qualley]], and [[Guy Pearce]], and follows the survivors of a [[global flu pandemic]] in rural [[Colorado]].

''The Dog Stars'' premiered at the [[Odeon Luxe Leicester Square]] on August 20, 2026, and was released in the United States by [[20th Century Studios]] on August 28. The film received mixed reviews from critics, and was a [[box-office bomb]], grossing only $39 million against a production budget of $70–110 million.

==Plot==
[[File:Cessna A185E Skywagon (N95LW, cn 185-1185) (4-12-2024).jpg|right|thumb|upright|alt=A red and white plane on a runway|A [[Cessna 185 Skywagon|Cessna A185E Skywagon]] [[Conventional landing gear|"tail-dragger"]], the type of plane Hig flies in the movie.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mahy |first1=Euan |title=Guernsey registered plane in latest Hollywood film |url=https://www.islandfm.com/news/guernsey/guernsey-registered-plane-in-latest-hollywood-film/ |website=Island FM |access-date=14 September 2026 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829010423/https://www.islandfm.com/news/guernsey/guernsey-registered-plane-in-latest-hollywood-film/ |archive-date=29 August 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2-MMWD - Cessna A185E Skywagon [18501996] - Flightradar24 |url=https://www.flightradar24.com/data/aircraft/2-mmwd |website=Flightradar24 |access-date=14 September 2026 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260915124052/https://www.flightradar24.com/data/aircraft/2-mmwd |archive-date=15 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> (In the original novel he flies a 1956 [[Cessna 182 Skylane|Cessna 182]] with [[tricycle landing gear]].)]]
<!-- Per WP:FILMPLOT, plot summary should be between 400 to 700 words. -->
In 2035,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Kyle |date=2026-08-27 |title=‘The Dog Stars’ Review: Finding Friends in Ridley Scott’s Post-Apocalypse |url=https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/film/the-dog-stars-review-finding-friends-in-ridley-scotts-post-apocalypse-2fc3a719 |access-date=2026-09-05 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660 |archive-date=30 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830075200/https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/film/the-dog-stars-review-finding-friends-in-ridley-scotts-post-apocalypse-2fc3a719 |url-status=live}}</ref> many years after a devastating [[global flu pandemic|flu pandemic]] almost eradicated humanity, Hig, a former mechanic, lives in [[Erie, Colorado]], with a dog named Jasper, and Bangley, a former Marine turned [[survivalist]]. Hig occasionally pilots a small [[propeller plane]] into a depopulated Denver to gather supplies of fuel and food. To Bangley's chagrin, Hig also supplies a nearby [[Mennonite]] community with food and occasional mechanical repairs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Yang |first=Katrina |title=Ridley Scott's Post-apocalyptic Sci-fi Movie Sets 2026 Release Date |url=https://screenrant.com/the-dog-stars-movie-release-date-confirmed/ |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=15 October 2025 |date=23 May 2025 |archive-date=23 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723235137/https://screenrant.com/the-dog-stars-movie-release-date-confirmed/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

When two teenage strangers approach, Bangley shoots them dead from his distance look-out point, creating a conflict with the more sympathetic Hig. While flying his propeller plane, Hig picks up a radio signal originating from [[Grand Junction, Colorado]], that suggests human life there. He has picked up this signal multiple times throughout the years since the pandemic, but always quickly lost contact.

While sleeping outside one day, Hig and Jasper encounter a large group trying to ambush their home. The two fight them off until Bangley appears to help them; Jasper is killed.  

Heartbroken, Hig decides he must find the source of the Grand Junction radio signal. Bangley, who does not approve of the journey, stays behind in Erie. After experiencing a mechanical failure, Hig lands in a valley where a father and daughter, Pops and Cima, live. The two form an uneasy alliance with Hig, as he repairs his plane and cuts down trees to make a [[runway]]. Hig starts a romantic relationship with Cima, who asks him to stay with them.

After their farm is raided in an attack, Hig, Cima, and Pops flee on Hig's plane. They make it to [[Grand Junction Regional Airport]], where the radio operator hesitantly allows them to land and enter their community unarmed. Theirs is the first to arrive in two years.

Upon arrival, the three are uneasy. Darlene, a former flight attendant who is the leader of the community, orders Cima to marry a soldier, due to her previous medical education. As Hig, Cima and Pops escape the airport, they discover the community's [[cannibalism]]. As they fly away, they bomb the Grand Junction airport terminal with [[grenades]] from the air.

The three fly back to Erie to check on Bangley, where they discover a major attack occurred at the airfield. Bangley managed to take out the over 30 attackers. He is injured but alive, so reluctantly comes with them to the Mennonite community to join an established new settlement there.

==Cast==
{{castlist|
* [[Jacob Elordi]] as Hig, a civilian pilot living with his dog
* [[Josh Brolin]] as Bangley, an aloof, gun-toting former Marine and Hig's companion
* [[Margaret Qualley]] as Cima, a young medic and Hig's love interest
* [[Guy Pearce]] as Jack / "Pops", a former [[Navy SEAL]] and Cima's father
* [[Allison Janney]] as Darlene, a former stewardess running a reconverted airport
* [[Benedict Wong]] as Aaron, the leader of a [[Mennonite]] group in the mountains
* [[Ewen Bremner]] as the Crossbow Hunter
* [[Sam Spruell]] as John
* [[Sai Bennett]] as Melissa
}}

==Production==
===Development===
[[File:Cinema Astra The Dog Stars.jpg|thumb|upright|''The Dog Stars'' movie poster in Italy]]
In November 2024, [[Ridley Scott]] stated that after shooting his planned [[Bee Gees]] biopic, he wanted to direct a then-unrevealed [[sci-fi]] film, adding that "it's already written".<ref>{{cite web |last=Lambie |first=Ryan |url=https://filmstories.co.uk/news/ridley-scott-says-hes-directing-a-mystery-sci-fi-film-exclusive/ |title=Ridley Scott Says He's Directing a Mystery Sci-fi Film |website=Film Stories |date=1 November 2024 |access-date=1 November 2024}}</ref> This project was later revealed to be based on [[Peter Heller (writer)|Peter Heller]]'s 2012 novel ''[[The Dog Stars]]'', adapted by [[Mark L. Smith]] and [[Christopher Wilkinson]]; only Smith received final credit for the screenplay.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bergesen |first1=Samantha |title=Jacob Elordi in Talks to Replace Paul Mescal in Ridley Scott's ''The Dog Stars'' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/jacob-elordi-replace-paul-mescal-ridley-scott-the-dog-stars-1235082999/ |website=[[IndieWire]] |date=7 January 2025 |access-date=8 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="WGA">{{cite web|url=https://directories.wga.org/project/1270000/the-dog-stars|title=''The Dog Stars''|publisher=[[Writers Guild of America West]]|date=August 6, 2025|access-date=April 10, 2026|archive-date=22 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260822234429/https://directories.wga.org/project/1270000/the-dog-stars|url-status=live}}</ref> By this time, it was set to be Scott's next film, with filming set to begin in spring 2025.<ref name="Kroll-2024">{{cite web |last1=Kroll |first1=Justin |last2=Fleming Jr |first2=Mike |title=Ridley Scott Back in Arena with ''Gladiator II'' Star Paul Mescal on ''The Dog Stars'' at 20th Century |url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/ridley-scott-paul-mescal-the-dog-stars-gladiator-ii-1236161226/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |access-date=8 November 2024 |date=8 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Stephan |first=Katcy |title=Ridley Scott and Paul Mescal to Re-Team After ''Gladiator II'' on ''The Dog Stars'' |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/ridley-scott-paul-mescal-the-dog-stars-1236205008/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=8 November 2024 |date=8 November 2024 |archive-date=8 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241108221122/https://variety.com/2024/film/news/ridley-scott-paul-mescal-the-dog-stars-1236205008/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

F**k It': Ridley Scott Reveals the Truth of What Happened with the ''Kingdom of Heaven'' Director's Cut |url=https://collider.com/ridley-scott-kingdom-of-heaven-directors-cut-blade-runner/ |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=15 October 2025 |date=7 June 2025 |archive-date=22 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251122165442/https://collider.com/ridley-scott-kingdom-of-heaven-directors-cut-blade-runner/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Scenes were also shot at [[Pinewood Studios]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pinewood Studios |date=April 29, 2026 |title=Watch the new trailer for ''The Dog Stars'', directed by Ridley Scott and starring Jacob Elordi, Josh Brolin, and Margaret Qualley with scenes  Shot at Pinewood. In cinemas August 28. |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DXtfJo1iCgK/?hl=en |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=Instagram}}</ref>

==Release==
''The Dog Stars'' premiered at the [[Odeon Luxe Leicester Square]] in London on August 20, 2026, and was released in the United States on August 28, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garner |first=Glenn |date=August 20, 2026 |title=''The Dog Stars'' World Premiere Red Carpet: Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, Rak the Dog and More |url=https://deadline.com/gallery/the-dog-stars-world-premiere-red-carpet-jacob-elordi-margaret-qualley-rak-the-dog-more/ |access-date=August 27, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US |archive-date=20 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260820223725/https://deadline.com/gallery/the-dog-stars-world-premiere-red-carpet-jacob-elordi-margaret-qualley-rak-the-dog-more/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2025/12/disney-release-dates-gatto-ready-or-not-2-dog-stars-1236655242/|title=Disney Moves Around ''Ready or Not 2'', ''The Dog Stars'' and Pixar’s ''Gatto'' in 2026 and 2027 Release Calendars|last=D'Alessandro|first=Anthony|date=December 22, 2025|access-date=December 22, 2025|archive-date=23 December 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251223113502/https://deadline.com/2025/12/disney-release-dates-gatto-ready-or-not-2-dog-stars-1236655242/|url-status=live}}</ref> It was previously scheduled for March 27, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grobar |first=Matt |date=May 22, 2025 |title=Disney Pushes Next Two ''Avengers'' Movies; Dates ''The Dog Stars'' & ''The Devil Wears Prada 2'' |url=https://deadline.com/2025/05/next-avengers-movies-push-release-dates-dog-stars-devil-wears-prada-1236409088/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522230719/https://deadline.com/2025/05/next-avengers-movies-push-release-dates-dog-stars-devil-wears-prada-1236409088/ |archive-date=May 22, 2025 |access-date=May 22, 2025 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Angelique |last2=Saperstein |first2=Pat |title=''The Devil Wears Prada'' Sequel Set for May 2026; Ridley Scott's ''The Dog Stars'' Dated for March |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/devil-wears-prada-2-may-2026-dog-stars-1236064250/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=16 October 2025 |date=22 May 2025 |archive-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011183141/https://variety.com/2025/film/news/devil-wears-prada-2-may-2026-dog-stars-1236064250/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
{{As of|2026|9|20|df=US}}, ''The Dog Stars'' has grossed $15 million in the United States and Canada, and $24 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $39 million.<ref name="NUM"/><ref name="BOM"/>

In the United States and Canada, ''The Dog Stars'' was released alongside ''[[Buddy (2026 film)|Buddy]]'', ''[[Coyote vs. Acme]]'', ''[[Legend of the White Dragon]]'' and ''[[Idiots (2026 film)|Idiots]]'', and was projected to gross $10–14 million from 3,300 theaters in its opening weekend.<ref name="preview">{{cite web |title= ''Coyote vs. Acme'' and ''Dog Stars'' Barking Up ''Spider-Man'''s Tree with Summer End Near – Weekend Preview |website= [[Deadline Hollywood]] |date= August 26, 2026 |url= https://deadline.com/2026/08/coyote-vs-acme-dog-stars-jacob-elordi-spider-man-box-office-1237051826/ |access-date= August 27, 2026 |archive-date= 27 August 2026 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260827171708/https://deadline.com/2026/08/coyote-vs-acme-dog-stars-jacob-elordi-spider-man-box-office-1237051826/ |url-status= live |last=D'Alessandro|first=Anthony}}</ref> The film ended up underperforming, debuting at $8 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=2026-08-30 |title=Box Office: 'Spider-Man' No. 1, 'Coyote Vs. Acme' $12M+, 'Dog Stars' Tanks |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/box-office-coyote-vs-acme-dog-stars-spider-man-1237061934/ |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US |archive-date=29 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829234434/https://deadline.com/2026/08/box-office-coyote-vs-acme-dog-stars-spider-man-1237061934/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Critical response===
{{RT prose|41|5.5|222|A derivative and drowsy tour through the post-apocalypse, ''The Dog Stars''{{'}} lush visuals can't compensate for its listless narrative and underpowered pacing.|ref=y|access-date=October 25, 2026}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 49 out of 100, based on 46 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''The Dog Stars'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-dog-stars |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=August 29, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260901030728/https://www.metacritic.com/movie/the-dog-stars/ |archive-date=1 September 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "C+" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=2026-08-29 |title=''Spider-Man'' Nearing $900M; ''Coyote vs. Acme'' Solid $14M Debut & 'A' CinemaScore, ''Dog Stars'' Going to the Dogs |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/box-office-coyote-vs-acme-dog-stars-spider-man-1237061934/ |access-date=2026-08-29 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US |archive-date=29 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829234434/https://deadline.com/2026/08/box-office-coyote-vs-acme-dog-stars-spider-man-1237061934/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Robert Daniels of ''[[RogerEbert.com]]'' gave the film one and a half out of four stars, writing, "It probably takes more effort to make a boring post-apocalyptic survivalist action film than to make a good one. If that's the case, then Ridley Scott must've been working overtime on ''The Dog Stars''."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-dog-stars-jacob-elordi-josh-brolin-margaret-qualley-ridley-scott-film-review-2026|title=''The Dog Stars''|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]|first=Robert|last=Daniels|date=August 2026|access-date=29 August 2026|archive-date=29 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829064206/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/the-dog-stars-jacob-elordi-josh-brolin-margaret-qualley-ridley-scott-film-review-2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Guy Lodge of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' wrote, "Somewhat aptly released at the tail end of a long, loud movie summer, this is a surprisingly low-energy, low-incident blockbuster; you'd appreciate its mellow, character-oriented approach if it gave you any real characters to hold onto."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2026/film/reviews/the-dog-stars-review-jacob-elordi-1236839483/|title=''The Dog Stars'' Review: Jacob Elordi's Sensitive Survivalist Can't Sustain a Dreary Dystopian Adventure|first=Guy|last=Lodge|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=August 25, 2026|access-date=August 29, 2026|archive-date=30 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830044059/https://variety.com/2026/film/reviews/the-dog-stars-review-jacob-elordi-1236839483/|url-status=live}}</ref> David Rooney of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' was more positive, writing, "Muted but never dull, ''The Dog Stars'' seems unlikely to land near the top of anyone's Ridley Scott rankings. But it's an appealingly mellow watch, even if that might seem antithetical to a post-apocalyptic drama positioned squarely in the shadow of death."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/the-dog-stars-review-jacob-elordi-ridley-scott-1236680319/|title=''The Dog Stars'' Review: Jacob Elordi and Margaret Qualley in Ridley Scott’s Subdued but Pleasingly Soulful Dystopian Western|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|first=David|last=Rooney|date=August 25, 2026|access-date=August 29, 2026|archive-date=30 August 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830023152/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/the-dog-stars-review-jacob-elordi-ridley-scott-1236680319/|url-status=live}}</ref>
